title: cmd_send has no atomic claim on approved rows -- duplicate emails to the same company
detail: cmd_send (lines 237-275) does SELECT ... where status='approved' ... limit cap, then loops calling the Gmail API, and only AFTER a successful send updates status='sent'. Two failure scenarios send the same row twice. (a) Concurrent runs: two invocations of 'python tools/outreach.py send' (operator + a second terminal, or an overlapping cron) both SELECT the same approved rows before either has updated them; each sends every row via Gmail, then both UPDATE to 'sent'. Invariant 5 (uq_outreach_one_touch) never fires because both sends are the SAME row -- the index constrains rows, not Gmail calls. The company receives two identical emails. (b) Crash window: Gmail accepts the message, then the db.run status update fails (dbconn.Db.run retries once on OperationalError then raises -- exactly the Supabase pooler drop dbconn.py documents as common) or the process is killed; the row stays 'approved' and the NEXT send run re-sends it. Fix shape: claim each row first with UPDATE outreach SET status='sending' WHERE id=%s AND status='approved' RETURNING id, and only call Gmail on a successful claim.
why_real: Verified against source. cmd_send (tools/outreach.py:226-279) selects approved rows with a plain SELECT (lines 237-244, no FOR UPDATE/SKIP LOCKED/claim step), calls the Gmail API (259-260), and only afterward marks the row 'sent' in a separate transaction (267-274); each Db.run is its own committed transaction (dbconn.py:66-95). (a) Two concurrent runs both see the same approved rows before either updates, both send via Gmail, and both UPDATE the same row id — uq_outreach_one_touch (sql/20_outreach.sql:60-62) is a partial unique index on outreach(entity_id) that constrains row count per entity, so updating one existing row can never violate it; nothing else serializes the runs. (b) If the post-send status update fails (Db.run retries once on OperationalError then raises — dbconn.py:73-89 — and dbconn.py's docstring documents Supabase pooler drops as the recurring real-world failure) or the process is killed in that window, the row stays 'approved' and the next send run re-selects and re-sends it. The proposed claim-first fix (UPDATE ... SET status='sending' WHERE id=%s AND status='approved' RETURNING id, committed before calling Gmail) genuinely closes (a) and downgrades (b) from duplicate email to a stuck 'sending' row. Only nit: cmd_send actually spans lines 226-279, not 237-275 — immaterial.

title: Ambiguous send exceptions marked 'failed' re-open Invariant 5 -- second email after a delivered-but-errored send
detail: In cmd_send, ANY exception from svc.users().messages().send() marks the row status='failed' (lines 261-265). sql/20_outreach.sql comments assume failed means "Gmail said no", but the except clause also catches unknown-outcome errors: a read timeout or connection reset AFTER Gmail accepted the message, an HTTP 5xx where googleapiclient's internal retry already delivered it, etc. Both the partial unique index (status not in ('cancelled','failed'), sql/20_outreach.sql lines 60-62) and cmd_draft's NOT EXISTS filter (lines 135-137) exclude 'failed' rows, so the entity becomes draftable again: draft -> approve -> send produces a SECOND outbound email to a company that already received the first. Invariant 5's "one touch per company, forever" does not hold across ambiguous failures. Only errors that provably mean not-sent (e.g. 4xx from the API with no message id) should be classed 'failed'; unknown outcomes need a distinct terminal state that the index still counts as a touch until a human clears it.
why_real: Verified against source. outreach.py lines 258-265: bare `except Exception` around svc.users().messages().send().execute() marks the row status='failed' for ANY error, including ambiguous outcomes (read timeout or connection reset after Gmail accepted the non-idempotent POST; the gmail_message_id is never captured). sql/20_outreach.sql lines 60-62: the Invariant 5 partial unique index excludes status in ('cancelled','failed'), so a failed row does not occupy the one-touch slot. outreach.py lines 135-137: cmd_draft's NOT EXISTS guard likewise excludes 'failed', and the entity stays 'shortlisted' because the exception path `continue`s before the entities update (lines 272-274). Therefore after a delivered-but-errored send the entity is re-draftable: draft -> approve -> send produces a second outbound email to a company that already received one, and the DB-level invariant the schema comments claim ("every layer above can be buggy and the invariant still holds") does not hold for unknown-outcome errors. Minor inaccuracy that doesn't affect the verdict: execute() defaults to num_retries=0, so googleapiclient's internal 5xx retry isn't active by default — but the lost-response timeout and httplib2's transport-level socket-error retry both realize the delivered-yet-excepted case. The suggested remedy (a distinct terminal state for unknown outcomes that the index still counts as a touch) is sound.

title: daily_send_cap is per-invocation only -- N runs per day sends N x cap
detail: Line 236: cap = min(int(cfg.get('daily_send_cap', 20)), args.limit). This caps one process invocation; nothing anywhere queries how many outreach rows have sent_at on the current date (grep confirms no sent_at::date / current_date accounting in the repo). Concrete scenario: an operator runs send in the morning, a scheduled job runs it again at noon, someone re-runs it after a 'failed' batch -- 3 runs x cap 20 = 60 emails in one day against a stated cap of 20, trivially tripping Gmail sending heuristics and the CAN-SPAM posture the config cares about. The module docstring (line 17) calls it a "daily ... hard ceiling" while config guidance says "per send run" -- the code implements neither a daily ceiling nor protection against overlapping runs. Fix: before sending, count rows where direction='outbound' and status='sent' and sent_at::date = current_date and subtract from cap.
why_real: Confirmed against source. tools/outreach.py:236 computes cap = min(daily_send_cap, --limit) and lines 237-244 select up to cap approved rows with no accounting of rows already sent today; each send flips rows to status='sent' (line 269), so every new invocation gets a fresh full cap. Grep confirms the only sent_at reads repo-wide are UI ordering (app/main.py:306) and a planned BUILD_PLAN item — no current_date/date_trunc daily accounting exists anywhere, and uq_outreach_one_touch bounds per-company-ever, not per-day. The 3-runs x cap-20 = 60 emails/day scenario genuinely occurs whenever >cap approved drafts exist (drafts accumulate across days), and a post-'failed' re-run sends fresh approved rows since failed rows are excluded. There is also no FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so truly concurrent runs can even double-send the same rows. Minor quibble only: the docstring (lines 10, 17) actually frames the ceiling per-run ('capped per run', 'the run: ... hard ceiling'), matching config guidance, so 'implements neither' overstates it slightly — the real defect is that the key name daily_send_cap promises daily semantics nothing implements. Core failure scenario stands as described; the proposed fix (subtract count of outbound/sent rows with sent_at::date = current_date) is sound.

title: Withdrawn approval can still be sent (cancel/send TOCTOU), and the post-send UPDATE has no status guard
detail: cmd_send materializes the whole approved batch up front (lines 237-244), then sends serially -- a batch of 20 Gmail calls takes real wall-clock time. If a human clicks 'Withdraw approval' in the UI (app/main.py outreach_decide 'cancel', lines 343-346, sets status='cancelled' where status in ('drafted','approved')) while the run is in flight, the already-selected row is sent anyway: there is no per-row re-check of status immediately before the Gmail call, and the success UPDATE at lines 267-271 is 'where id=%s' with no 'and status=approved' predicate, so it silently flips the human's 'cancelled' back to 'sent'. Result: an email goes out that the human explicitly un-approved, with no trace that a withdrawal happened. The same atomic-claim fix as the double-send finding (UPDATE ... WHERE status='approved' RETURNING before calling Gmail) closes this window to milliseconds.
why_real: Confirmed by re-derivation. cmd_send (tools/outreach.py:236-244) materializes all approved rows in one committed transaction (Db.run in tools/dbconn.py commits per call; no FOR UPDATE, no lock held during the loop), then sends serially with no per-row status re-check before the Gmail call (lines 250-260 check only email presence and email_status from the stale SELECT). The UI cancel (app/main.py:343-346) sets status='cancelled' where status in ('drafted','approved') and commits on an independent connection, so it succeeds mid-run. The success UPDATE (outreach.py:267-271) is 'where id=%s' with no status predicate, so it overwrites the human's 'cancelled' with 'sent', erasing any trace of the withdrawal. Window is wide (serial Gmail API calls across up to cap=min(daily_send_cap, --limit) rows, default 20). The suggested atomic-claim fix (UPDATE ... WHERE status='approved' RETURNING before the Gmail call) would close it.

title: No placeholder/content validation after the draft stage -- edited drafts and stale SET_ME drafts can be sent
detail: render() in tools/outreach.py (lines 105-112) is the ONLY unfilled-placeholder check, and it runs at draft time only. Two bypasses: (1) PATCH /api/outreach/{oid} (app/main.py lines 315-329) accepts arbitrary subject/body with no {{...}} scan and no non-empty check -- a reviewer who pastes template text containing {{company}} into the edit box (or clears the body) and clicks Approve gets it sent verbatim by cmd_send, which performs no final validation. (2) The send-time SET_ME refusal (tools/outreach.py lines 233-234) inspects the CURRENT config, not the row being sent: drafts rendered while sender was still SET_ME contain the literal text 'SET_ME e.g. Arunabh Kumar' / 'SET_ME street address for the email footer (CAN-SPAM)' in their bodies; once someone fixes the config, the check passes and those stale approved drafts send with the sentinel text -- the guard protects the wrong object. Also, render()'s leftover regex r'{{\w+}}' misses variants like '{{ company }}' or '{{first-name}}' in a config template, which then ship silently. Cheap fix: re-run the leftover-placeholder scan (plus a SET_ME scan) per row inside cmd_send and skip/flag offenders.
why_real: Verified against source. (1) PATCH /api/outreach/{oid} (app/main.py:315-329) writes arbitrary subject/body via coalesce with only a status='drafted' guard — no {{...}} scan, no non-empty check (empty string is non-NULL and is stored); approve (main.py:340-342) flips status without content inspection, and cmd_send (tools/outreach.py:250-257) sends the row verbatim via MIMEText(body), checking only contact presence and email_status != 'invalid'. (2) The send-time SET_ME refusal (tools/outreach.py:233-234) inspects the CURRENT config (json.dumps(cfg.get("sender"))), not the row bodies; cmd_draft (lines 122-126, 152-158) renders drafts containing the literal config sentinels — the exact strings 'SET_ME e.g. Arunabh Kumar' and 'SET_ME street address for the email footer (CAN-SPAM)' exist in sql/03*.sql and config/segment.us-production-houses.json — so once config is fixed, stale approved drafts pass the check and send with sentinel text; the guard protects the wrong object (does require a human having approved such a draft, which the finding acknowledges). (3) render()'s regex r"{{\w+}}" (line 109) misses '{{ company }}' and '{{first-name}}' since \w excludes spaces/hyphens, and the replace() fill also skips them, so variant placeholders in a DB-config template ship silently. Repo-wide grep confirms render() is the only placeholder check (draft-time only) and cmd_send has no final content validation. All cited line numbers match.

title: Recipient address is neither snapshotted at approval nor validated at send -- wrong-address and multi-recipient paths
detail: cmd_send addresses the live 'c.email' from a join on o.contact_id at SEND time (lines 238-244, 256), not the address the human saw when approving. Scenario A (wrong address): an enrichment re-run or manual fix updates that contact row's email between approval and send; the approved text goes to an address no human ever reviewed, with a greeting derived from the old data. Scenario B (multi-recipient/header issues): contacts.email is unvalidated TEXT (sql/01_schema.sql line 68, no CHECK) populated from Apollo/scrapes, and cmd_send puts it straight into msg['to'] on a compat32 MIMEText with no single-address validation -- a value like 'info@x.com, press@x.com' delivers to BOTH addresses (Gmail API sends raw RFC822 to all To: recipients), and a value containing CR/LF injects extra headers (e.g. Bcc). Note the invalid-email guard (line 253) only skips email_status == 'invalid' exactly; it does nothing about a syntactically mangled or multi-address string on a 'valid'/'unverified' row, so it is not a defense here. Fix: snapshot the recipient into the outreach row at draft time, show it at approval, send only to that value, and validate it as exactly one RFC-5322 addr-spec before building the message.
why_real: Verified against source. (1) No snapshot: the outreach table (sql/20_outreach.sql) has no recipient column — cmd_draft (tools/outreach.py:165-168) stores only entity_id/contact_id/template_key/subject/body. (2) cmd_send (lines 237-244, 256) resolves c.email via a live join on o.contact_id at send time and puts it into msg['to'] unvalidated; the approval UI's outreach_folders view also live-joins c.email, so a post-approval UPDATE to contacts.email (manual SQL fixes are an explicit workflow here) sends the approved text — including the greeting rendered from old data — to an address no human reviewed. Nuance: the repo's automated enrichment scripts use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (new rows, not in-place email updates), so 'enrichment re-run' is a weaker trigger than claimed, but the manual-fix path and the structural gap are real. (3) Multi-address confirmed empirically: contacts.email is bare TEXT with no CHECK (01_schema.sql:68), MIMEText serializes 'info@x.com, press@x.com' cleanly into To:, and Gmail API raw send delivers to all To: recipients; the line-253 guard only matches email_status=='invalid' exactly. (4) One sub-claim overstated: CR/LF header injection does NOT occur — tested on Python 3.10, compat32 Header.encode raises HeaderParseError on embedded-header values (\n, \r\n, and bare \r variants), so the real outcome is an unhandled crash at msg.as_bytes() (line 257, outside the try block), killing the send run rather than injecting a Bcc. Core finding and both named paths (wrong-address, multi-recipient) genuinely occur; the fix proposed (snapshot at draft, show at approval, validate one addr-spec at send) targets verified gaps.

title: Skipped approved rows permanently occupy cap slots -- send pipeline can silently starve to zero
detail: cmd_send's SELECT is 'order by o.created_at limit %s' with the cap applied at selection (lines 237-244), and rows skipped in the loop (contact vanished, email_status='invalid', lines 251-254) are left in status='approved' with no state change. They are therefore re-selected at the head of the queue on every run, each one consuming a cap slot that a sendable row behind it never gets. Concrete scenario: with cap 20, once 20 old approved rows have invalid/vanished contacts, every future run selects exactly those 20, skips all of them, and reports '0 sent (cap 20)' forever -- newer approved drafts never send and nothing surfaces the deadlock except log lines. Skipped rows should be transitioned (e.g. back to 'drafted' or a 'blocked' state) or excluded in the WHERE clause, and the cap should count actual sends.
why_real: Confirmed in tools/outreach.py cmd_send. The SELECT (lines 237-244) applies the cap via LIMIT at selection time with 'order by o.created_at' ascending, so the oldest approved rows always fill the window. The skip branches (line 251-252 'contact vanished' when the left-joined contact email is NULL, and lines 253-254 email_status='invalid') only log and continue — no UPDATE — leaving the row status='approved' with an unchanged created_at, so it is re-selected at the head of the queue every run. Failed and sent rows do transition (lines 263-265, 267-274), so only skip-path rows recycle. Once stuck-row count reaches the cap, every run selects exactly those rows, skips them all, prints '0 sent (cap N)', and returns exit 0; newer approved drafts are starved forever. Bonus severity: cmd_draft's NOT EXISTS filter (lines 135-137) also blocks re-drafting for entities with a stuck 'approved' row. Partial slot-wasting begins with even one stuck row; total deadlock at cap stuck rows, exactly as claimed.

title: cmd_send can email the same company twice: no crash-safety between Gmail accept and the DB status update
detail: In cmd_send (lines 259-274) the Gmail API call executes first, and only afterwards does db.run() update the row to status='sent'. If that update fails (Db.run retries OperationalError exactly once, then raises - and dbconn.py's own docstring documents the Supabase pooler dropping connections mid-run three times in one day), or the operator hits Ctrl+C / the machine sleeps in that window, the process dies AFTER Gmail accepted the message while the row is still status='approved' with no gmail_message_id recorded. The next 'python tools/outreach.py send' selects the same row (where status='approved' order by created_at - it is at the head of the queue) and sends a second email to the same contact. Invariant 5's partial unique index cannot catch this: sending updates the existing row, it never inserts a second outbound row, so the DB-level 'one touch per company' guard does not cover duplicate SMTP sends. There is also no way to detect it happened afterwards. Fix direction: flip the row to an intermediate state (e.g. status='sending') and commit BEFORE calling messages().send(), so a crashed run leaves a visibly stuck row instead of a re-sendable approved one.
why_real: Re-derived from source. cmd_send (tools/outreach.py) calls Gmail messages().send().execute() at lines 258-260 and only then updates the row to status='sent' with gmail_message_id via db.run() at lines 267-274; the try/except at 261-266 covers only the Gmail call, so a failure in the post-send DB update (or Ctrl+C/sleep/power loss in that window) kills the process with the row still 'approved' and no gmail_message_id. Db.run (tools/dbconn.py lines 66-95) retries OperationalError exactly once then raises (and non-OperationalError exceptions like InterfaceError raise immediately), and dbconn.py's docstring documents three Supabase-pooler connection drops in one day (2026-08-29), making the failure realistic. The next send run's query (lines 237-244: where status='approved' and direction='outbound' order by created_at) re-selects the orphaned row at the head of the queue and re-sends the identical email. Invariant 5 (sql/20_outreach.sql lines 59-62) is a partial unique index on outreach(entity_id) for outbound rows and only fires on INSERT; cmd_send UPDATEs the existing row, so it cannot prevent the duplicate transmission. Afterwards the row is indistinguishable from a never-sent draft (approved, null sent_at/gmail_message_id), so the system has no way to detect the duplicate. Failure scenario occurs exactly as described.

title: cmd_pull ingests the owner's own follow-up messages as inbound prospect replies
detail: Line 295: 'for m in t.get("messages", [])[1:]' assumes only messages[0] is ours. Concrete scenario: prospect replies (thread message 2), the owner answers from the Gmail web UI (message 3). Message 3's id is not in outreach (only the FIRST send's gmail_message_id was stored), so the exists-check at line 297 passes and the owner's own email is inserted as direction='inbound', status='received'. It then shows in the Replies folder as if the prospect wrote it, and cmd_triage runs Claude over the owner's own enthusiastic BD text - which the prompt will classify 'positive', landing our own message in the Positive folder where a human can mark_positive it and move the entity to in_conversation on fake evidence. Fix: skip messages whose From header matches GMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS or whose labelIds contains 'SENT', instead of only slicing off index 0.
why_real: Verified against source. cmd_pull (tools/outreach.py:295) filters "our" messages solely by slicing off index 0; cmd_send (lines 267-271) stores gmail_message_id only for the initial API send, so an owner reply sent from the Gmail web UI (same account, appears in threads().get with a new id and SENT label) passes the exists-check (297-300) and is inserted as direction='inbound', status='received' — with the prospect's contact_id, so the UI attributes it to the prospect. It lands in the 'inbox' folder (sql/20_outreach.sql view; claim's "Replies folder" is a cosmetic naming difference), cmd_triage (355+) runs Claude on it and the prompt's positive criteria (wants a call / offers deck) match owner BD text, and app/main.py:347-356 lets a human mark_positive an inbound row, moving the entity contacted->in_conversation on the owner's own message. No From-header or labelIds check exists anywhere in the file; the proposed fix (skip From==GMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS or 'SENT' in labelIds) is sound and the needed data is already fetched.

title: Unsendable approved rows permanently occupy send-cap slots; queue wedges at zero sends
detail: cmd_send's skip paths (line 251-254: contact vanished, email_status='invalid') leave the row status='approved' untouched, and the selection query is 'where status=approved order by created_at limit cap' - so the SAME skipped rows are re-selected at the head of every run, each one consuming a cap slot. Once the number of permanently-skipped approved rows reaches the cap (default 20), every run selects only skips and prints '0 sent (cap 20)' forever, while newer approved drafts behind them are never reached. This is reachable: cmd_draft's query (line 128-139) only requires c.email is not null - it does NOT filter email_status - so drafts ARE created for contacts whose email already failed verification; and the outreach_folders view (sql/20_outreach.sql line 85-104) does not expose email_status, so the approver in the UI cannot see they are approving an unsendable draft. Skipped rows also hold the Invariant-5 index slot (approved is not in the ('cancelled','failed') exclusion), blocking any re-draft. Fix: mark perma-skips 'failed' with a send_error (freeing the index slot for a corrected re-draft), and/or exclude email_status='invalid' at draft time.
why_real: Re-derived from source: cmd_send (tools/outreach.py:237-244) selects 'where status=approved order by created_at limit cap' and its two skip paths (251-254, no-email and email_status='invalid') perform no DB write — unlike the Gmail-failure path (262-265) which sets status='failed'. Skipped rows therefore keep status='approved' and their original created_at, are re-selected at the queue head every run, and each consumes one of the cap slots; once the cap-many oldest approved rows are all unsendable, every run prints '0 sent' while newer approved drafts are never fetched. Reachability confirmed: cmd_draft (128-139) filters only c.email is not null, not email_status (schema 01_schema.sql:62-84 keeps email non-null when marked 'invalid', a legal CHECK value the P17 verifier flow writes), and contact_id is 'on delete set null' making the vanished-contact skip permanent. The approver is blind: outreach_folders (20_outreach.sql:85-104) omits email_status and the UI (app/main.py:300-313, 332-344) reads only that view with no sendability check on approve. The Invariant-5 partial unique index (20_outreach.sql:60-62) excludes only cancelled/failed, so the wedged approved row also blocks any re-draft (cmd_draft's not-exists clause + on conflict do nothing). Every element of the claim, including line numbers, matches the code.

title: cmd_pull's reply insert violates Db.run's idempotency contract - duplicate inbox rows on a retried commit
detail: Db.run (tools/dbconn.py line 66-95) retries fn once on OperationalError and its docstring states 'fn must be idempotent -- it may run twice if the connection dies after the work but before the commit lands.' The reply insert at outreach.py line 305-310 is a plain INSERT with no ON CONFLICT, and sql/20_outreach.sql has no unique index on gmail_message_id, so the only dedup is the separate exists-check that ran in an EARLIER transaction. Scenario: the insert commits on the server, the connection drops before the client sees it, Db.run retries, and the same Gmail message becomes two 'received' rows - both shown in the Replies folder and both burning a Claude call in triage. A unique index on gmail_message_id plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (as cmd_draft already does) closes it.
why_real: Verified against source. Db.run (tools/dbconn.py:66-95) wraps both fn(cur) and conn.commit() in one try, catches psycopg2.OperationalError, and re-runs fn once on a fresh connection — its docstring explicitly warns fn may run twice when the connection dies after the work but before the commit acknowledgment. cmd_pull's reply insert (tools/outreach.py:305-310) is a plain INSERT with no ON CONFLICT, and no unique index exists on gmail_message_id anywhere in sql/ (the only unique index on outreach, uq_outreach_one_touch, is partial WHERE direction='outbound', so inbound rows are unconstrained). The exists-check (outreach.py:297-299) runs in a separate, earlier db.run transaction and is not part of the retried fn, so on an ambiguous commit (COMMIT lands server-side, connection drops before the client sees it — the exact Supabase-pooler failure dbconn.py's header documents happening three times in one day) the retry inserts a second identical row. Both duplicate rows land in the inbox folder of the outreach_folders view (sql/20_outreach.sql:92-101, no dedup) and cmd_triage (outreach.py:355-357) selects every direction='inbound' status='received' row, so each duplicate costs a separate Anthropic API call. The proposed fix mirrors cmd_draft's existing pattern (on conflict do nothing at outreach.py:167 backed by a unique index) and would close the window. Minor nits only: the view names the folder 'inbox' not 'Replies', and the fix needs the unique index to be partial (WHERE gmail_message_id IS NOT NULL) since outbound drafts have NULL gmail_message_id — neither affects the finding's validity.

title: 'Withdraw approval' sends the row to a folder no UI pill shows - the draft silently vanishes
detail: The approved-state detail pane (app.js line 358-361) offers 'Withdraw approval' wired to action 'cancel', which main.py sets to status='cancelled'. The outreach_folders view maps cancelled to folder 'other' (sql/20_outreach.sql line 100), but the FOLDERS array in app.js (line 286-290) has no 'other' pill and the folder pills are the only navigation. Concrete: a user clicks Withdraw approval expecting the draft back in Drafts for re-editing; instead the row disappears from every visible folder and the text they approved is unreachable from the UI (only recoverable via SQL, or by re-running the draft command which renders a fresh draft, discarding any manual edits). Either map cancellation of an approved row back to status='drafted', or add the 'other'/'cancelled' folder to FOLDERS.
why_real: Verified end-to-end. app.js:358-361 renders 'Withdraw approval' for status='approved' and line 380 wires it to action 'cancel'; main.py:343-346 sets status='cancelled' (approved rows eligible); sql/20_outreach.sql:92-101 maps a cancelled outbound row (triage NULL — triage only settable on inbound rows) to folder 'other' via the else branch; app.js:286-290 FOLDERS has no 'other' pill and the pill bar is the only outreach navigation, with /api/outreach filtering strictly by folder=%s, so the row becomes unreachable from the UI (even its count is never rendered). Recovery detail also confirmed: tools/outreach.py:135-137 excludes cancelled rows from the one-touch check, so re-running draft renders a fresh template, discarding the edits saved on approve. The same vanishing applies to 'Cancel draft' on drafted rows, so the finding slightly understates the surface.

title: Send-before-record ordering can email the same company twice, defeating Invariant 5
detail: cmd_send (lines 259-275) calls the Gmail API first and only afterwards updates the row to 'sent'. Two concrete double-send paths: (1) Gmail accepts the message but the response is lost to a client-side timeout -- the except branch (lines 261-265) marks the row 'failed'; the partial unique index (sql/20_outreach.sql line 62) and cmd_draft's not-exists filter (line 137) both deliberately exclude 'failed', so the next draft run creates a fresh draft for that entity, a human approves it, and the company receives the email a second time. (2) Gmail accepts, then the process dies before the db.run update lands (Ctrl+C, or dbconn's two OperationalError attempts both fail against the Supabase pooler -- the exact failure mode documented in dbconn.py's header); the row stays 'approved' and the next `python tools/outreach.py send` run re-sends it, because the query at lines 237-244 selects it again. The unique index guarantees one outbound ROW per entity, not one delivered EMAIL; nothing claims the row (e.g. a 'sending' state written before the API call) so the at-most-once property the whole file is built around does not actually hold.
why_real: Re-derived from source: cmd_send's try (outreach.py:258-260) wraps only the Gmail API call; the status='sent' update (267-274) runs after, so send-before-record ordering is real. Path 1 confirmed: a client-side error after server-side accept hits the except branch (261-265) marking the row 'failed'; the partial unique index (sql/20_outreach.sql:60-62) and cmd_draft's not-exists filter (outreach.py:135-137) both exclude 'failed', and the entity stays 'shortlisted' (the 'contacted' update is success-branch only), so a fresh draft is created, approved by a human who was told the first send failed, and delivered a second time — no index conflict because the failed row left the index scope. Path 2 confirmed: the db.run at line 267 sits outside the try; a Ctrl+C or a double OperationalError (dbconn.py run retries once then re-raises — the documented Supabase pooler failure mode) leaves the row 'approved', and the next send run's query (237-244) selects status='approved' rows and re-sends the same row with no human intervention. No 'sending'/claim state exists (status check constraint, sql:38-47) and nothing is written before the API call, so the index enforces one outbound row, not one delivered email; at-most-once does not hold.

title: pull ingests the operator's own messages and Gmail drafts as inbound replies from the company
detail: cmd_pull line 295 iterates t.get("messages", [])[1:] -- it skips only the FIRST message and treats everything else in the thread as an inbound reply, with no check of the From header or labelIds. Concrete scenario: a BD person replies to a lead's reply directly from the Gmail web UI (the natural next step after marking a reply positive). The next pull run finds that message, its id matches no outreach row, and inserts it as direction='inbound', status='received', attributed to the company and contact (lines 305-310). cmd_triage then classifies OUR OWN pitch/follow-up text -- which by the prompt's own rubric ('wants a call, asks questions') will typically score 'positive' -- and it surfaces in the Positive folder as if the company said it. Worse, Gmail threads().get also returns unsent DRAFT messages, and a Gmail draft's message id changes on every save, so an operator composing a reply in Gmail across several pull runs produces a new bogus inbound row per run that the gmail_message_id dedupe can never catch. Filter messages whose From matches GMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS or whose labelIds contain SENT/DRAFT.
why_real: Confirmed from source. cmd_pull line 295 iterates t.get("messages", [])[1:] with only a positional skip of index 0; headers are read only for the subject (lines 302-303) and neither From nor labelIds is ever checked. Dedupe (lines 297-299) matches only gmail_message_id values recorded by cmd_send's API sends, so a reply the BD person sends from the Gmail web UI has an unrecorded id and is inserted at lines 305-310 as direction='inbound', status='received', attributed to the lead's entity/contact. Pull never updates the outbound row's status, so sent threads are re-polled every run. cmd_triage (lines 355-357) then classifies the company's own pitch text, which fits the prompt's positive rubric (wants a call, asks questions, asks for the deck). The draft sub-claim also holds: Gmail users.threads.get returns unsent drafts as thread messages (DRAFT label), and each draft autosave assigns a new message id, so composing in Gmail across pull runs yields one new bogus inbound row per run that the gmail_message_id dedupe cannot catch. The proposed fix (filter From == GMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS or labelIds containing SENT/DRAFT) targets exactly the missing check.

title: Reply insert is not idempotent: Db.run's retry (or concurrent pulls) duplicates inbound rows
detail: cmd_pull's dedupe is a check-then-insert across two separate transactions (SELECT at lines 297-299, INSERT at lines 305-310), and the INSERT has no `on conflict do nothing` while sql/20_outreach.sql defines no unique index on gmail_message_id. dbconn.Db.run explicitly retries the lambda once on OperationalError and documents 'fn must be idempotent -- it may run twice if the connection dies after the work but before the commit lands' (dbconn.py lines 66-71). Concrete scenario: the Supabase session pooler drops the connection while the reply INSERT's commit is in flight (the precise failure dbconn.py was written for -- it happened three times on 2026-08-29 per its header); the commit actually landed server-side, Db.run retries, and the same reply is inserted twice. Both copies appear in the inbox folder, triage classifies both, and marking one positive leaves its twin sitting in inbox as apparently-unhandled. The same duplication occurs if two pull runs overlap (both pass the exists check, both insert). cmd_draft protects itself with `on conflict do nothing` backed by the partial unique index; cmd_pull has no equivalent backstop -- add a unique index on gmail_message_id (where not null) plus `on conflict do nothing`.
why_real: Verified against source. cmd_pull (tools/outreach.py) does its dedupe as a SELECT in one Db.run transaction (lines 297-299) and the INSERT in a separate Db.run transaction (lines 305-310) with no ON CONFLICT clause; sql/20_outreach.sql defines no unique index on gmail_message_id (the only unique index, uq_outreach_one_touch, is partial on entity_id where direction='outbound', so inbound rows are unconstrained). Db.run (tools/dbconn.py lines 66-95) catches psycopg2.OperationalError — including one raised from conn.commit() while the commit is in flight — and re-runs the lambda once on a fresh connection; only the INSERT lambda is retried, not the exists check, so if the commit landed server-side before the pooler drop (the exact failure mode dbconn.py's header documents from 2026-08-29), the same reply row is inserted twice. The docstring's explicit idempotency requirement is violated. The concurrent-pulls race is also real: two runs both pass the exists check and both insert with nothing to conflict. Both duplicates fall into the outreach_folders 'inbox' folder and are both picked up by cmd_triage. Only minor imprecision: the twin might end up in the same triage folder rather than strictly 'inbox', but the core defect and both duplication paths occur exactly as described. cmd_draft's on-conflict-do-nothing backed by its unique index confirms the intended pattern is absent here.

title: Perpetually-skipped approved rows wedge the send queue (head-of-line blocking)
detail: The send query (lines 237-244) fetches the oldest `cap` approved rows (`order by o.created_at limit %s`), then skips rows whose contact vanished or whose email_status='invalid' (lines 251-254) WITHOUT transitioning them out of 'approved'. Those rows stay at the front of the created_at ordering forever. Concrete scenario: a verification pass marks 20 contacts invalid after their drafts were approved; with daily_send_cap=20 the query now fetches exactly those 20 rows every run, skips all of them, and sends nothing -- newer approved drafts are never even fetched, and every future run prints 20 SKIP lines and '0 sent'. Even below the cap, each stuck row permanently steals one slot of the fetch window. The skip conditions belong in the SQL WHERE clause, and/or the skipped rows should be moved to 'failed' with a send_error so a human sees them in the Failed folder instead of them silently occupying the outbox.
why_real: Verified against tools/outreach.py: the send query (lines 236-244) applies `order by o.created_at limit cap` in SQL before any filtering, and the skip paths (lines 251-254, missing contact or email_status='invalid') `continue` without any status transition — unlike the send-failure path (lines 261-265) which correctly moves rows to 'failed'. Skipped rows therefore remain 'approved' with their original created_at and re-occupy the same front-of-window slots every run. With 20 oldest approved rows invalidated and cap=20, the query fetches exactly those rows each run, skips all, sends 0, and never fetches newer approved rows — head-of-line blocking exactly as described. The scenario is reachable by design: 'invalid' is in the contacts CHECK constraint (sql/01_schema.sql), a P17 verification pass writes email_status post-contact-creation (docs/P10_runbook.md, sql/10_enrich_template.sql), and the file's docstring itself promises to refuse sends on failed verification. No automatic path rescues the rows (draft's NOT EXISTS excludes them; only manual UI cancel in app/main.py lines 344-345 does), and they sit unmarked in the 'outbox' folder (sql/20_outreach.sql line 94).

title: send ignores entity status: a company rejected after approval still gets emailed
detail: The send query (lines 237-244) filters only on outreach.status='approved' and joins entities purely for the name -- there is no condition on e.status. Concrete scenario: a draft is created and approved; before the next send run, the reviewer rejects the company in the review tab (POST /api/leads/{id}/decision with 'reject' -- e.g. a re-harvest surfaced 'they already refused us', the exact case Invariant 4 exists for). `python tools/outreach.py send` emails them anyway. The follow-on entity update (lines 272-274) then no-ops because it is guarded by `and status='shortlisted'`, so the rejected entity has a live sent thread while its status still says 'rejected' -- and any later reply marked positive also no-ops the in_conversation promotion (see the mark_positive guard in app/main.py line 356). The send loop should skip (or the query exclude) entities whose status is no longer shortlisted/contacted.
why_real: Confirmed by re-derivation from source. The send query (tools/outreach.py:237-244) filters only on o.status='approved' and o.direction='outbound', joining entities solely for e.name — no e.status condition. POST /api/leads/{id}/decision 'reject' (app/main.py:242-266) sets entities.status='rejected' with no guard on prior status and no cascade to outreach rows (verified: no DB trigger in sql/ touches outreach on entity status change; only updated_at/status_changed_at triggers exist). So an approved draft for a subsequently-rejected entity is selected and emailed; the only per-row skips are missing email and email_status='invalid'. Both claimed no-ops verify exactly: the post-send promotion (outreach.py:272-274) is guarded by "and status='shortlisted'" so the rejected entity keeps status 'rejected' with a live sent thread, and the mark_positive promotion (app/main.py:354-356, guard "and status='contacted'" at line 356) silently no-ops for a rejected entity. Invariant 5 (sql/20_outreach.sql:60-62) prevents duplicate touches only, and the re-import shield (Invariant 4) blocks harvest re-entry, not sends — nothing mitigates this path.

title: mark_positive silently fails to promote the entity, and the promotion is irreversible
detail: In outreach_decide (lines 347-359), the entity promotion is `update entities set status='in_conversation' ... where id=%s and status='contacted'` (lines 354-356) and the endpoint returns {"ok": true} whether or not that update matched. Concrete scenario A (stranded short of the goal state): the entity never reached 'contacted' -- e.g. the reviewer hit Undo/reject between shortlist and send so cmd_send's `where status='shortlisted'` guard no-oped (tools/outreach.py line 274). A human marks the reply positive, gets 'done', the reply moves to the Positive folder, but the company never enters in_conversation -- the state the endpoint's own docstring calls the reason the engine exists -- and nothing anywhere reports it. Concrete scenario B (stranded past it): a misclick on Mark positive promotes the entity to in_conversation; clicking Mark negative afterwards flips the reply's triage label but performs no entity demotion, and the leads UI renders its Undo button only when status is 'shortlisted' or 'rejected' (app.js lines 237-238), so there is no UI path out of in_conversation at all. The row count of the entity update should at minimum be checked and surfaced.
why_real: Verified against source. main.py:354-356 promotes the entity with `where id=%s and status='contacted'` and never checks rowcount; line 359 returns {"ok": true} unconditionally (the branch's only 409 covers non-inbound rows, not the entity update). Scenario A reproduces: the decide endpoint (main.py:242-266) has no status guard so Undo/reject can land between approval and send; cmd_send (tools/outreach.py:242) selects only on outreach status='approved' with no entity-status filter, sends the mail, and its entity promotion `where ... status='shortlisted'` (line 273-274) silently no-ops — leaving a 'sent' outreach whose entity never reaches 'contacted'; a later mark_positive triages the reply into the Positive folder (sql/20_outreach.sql:97) and toasts "done" while the in_conversation promotion matches zero rows, unreported. Scenario B reproduces: mark_negative after a misclicked mark_positive succeeds (outreach update guarded only by direction='inbound') but the endpoint has no demotion code; app.js:237-238 renders Undo only for 'shortlisted'/'rejected', and an in_conversation entity is unreachable in the leads UI at all (filterQuery never sets status, so /api/leads defaults to OPEN_STATUSES, main.py:41/151-152, which excludes in_conversation; shortlist tab shows only 'shortlisted'; outreach tab has no link to the lead panel) — so even the unguarded Shortlist/Reject buttons cannot be reached. Both failure scenarios occur exactly as described.

title: Cancelled rows land in folder 'other', which the UI never lists -- 'Withdraw approval' makes the row vanish with its edits
detail: The outreach_folders view maps status='cancelled' to folder 'other' (sql/20_outreach.sql line 100), but the UI's FOLDERS array (app.js lines 286-290) has no 'other' entry and /api/outreach only ever serves one named folder, so a cancelled row is unreachable from every screen. Concrete scenario: a reviewer notices a typo in an approved draft and clicks 'Withdraw approval' (app.js line 359), reasonably expecting the row back in Drafts for editing. The endpoint sets status='cancelled' (main.py lines 344-346) -- a terminal state with no transition back to 'drafted' -- and the row disappears from all seven folders. Their hand-edited subject/body (edited pre-approval via the PATCH-on-approve flow) is gone from view; the only recovery is re-running `python tools/outreach.py draft`, which regenerates the template text without their edits. Either 'Withdraw approval' should return the row to 'drafted', or a Cancelled folder should exist so the text remains recoverable.
why_real: Verified end-to-end against source. sql/20_outreach.sql line 100: outbound cancelled rows (triage always NULL for outbound) fall to the `else 'other'` folder. app.js lines 286-290: the FOLDERS array has seven entries with no 'other', the folder bar is built only from it, and main.py's /api/outreach serves one named folder per request — so cancelled rows (and even their count, dropped by `d.counts[key] || 0`) are unreachable from every screen. app.js lines 358-359/380: 'Withdraw approval' posts action=cancel; main.py lines 343-346 set status='cancelled', and no API transition leaves that state (approve and PATCH-edit require 'drafted', cancel requires drafted/approved, mark_* requires inbound) — terminal as claimed. The hand edits were persisted by the PATCH-on-approve flow (app.js 366-371) but become invisible. Recovery path confirmed too: tools/outreach.py cmd_draft's NOT EXISTS excludes status in ('cancelled','failed') and the entity stays 'shortlisted', so re-drafting works but renders fresh template text (lines 151-168), discarding the edits. Only nuance: the edited text survives in the DB (recoverable via SQL or a manual ?folder=other request), but the finding claims UI unreachability, which is exactly accurate.

title: pull aborts the whole run on the first thread fetch error, blocking later threads' replies
detail: The threads().get call at line 294 is not wrapped in try/except. Concrete scenario: the operator deletes one outreach email from the Gmail mailbox (or the thread otherwise 404s); every subsequent `pull` run raises on that thread and dies before reaching the threads iterated after it, so replies from every company later in the scan order are never ingested until someone diagnoses the traceback. One bad thread should be logged and skipped, not fatal.
why_real: Confirmed from source: in cmd_pull, svc.users().threads().get(...).execute() at line 294 of tools/outreach.py has no try/except, and no handler exists upstream (main() dispatches directly, __main__ does sys.exit(main())). Any HttpError (404 from a permanently deleted thread, or transient 429/5xx — execute() has no default retries) propagates, killing the run mid-loop before later threads are processed, and before db.close()/the summary log. The failing row keeps status='sent' so the same thread is re-fetched and re-raises on every subsequent pull, persistently blocking reply ingestion for all threads iterated after it. This is also inconsistent with the file's own pattern: cmd_send (lines 258–266) and cmd_triage (lines 362–372) both wrap their per-item API calls in try/except and continue. Minor caveat: a simple move-to-trash does not 404 the thread — permanent deletion does — but the claim hedges with "or the thread otherwise 404s" and the abort behavior holds for any per-thread error.

title: Detail panel goes stale after approve/cancel; edits made after approving are never saved but the approved (unedited) text still sends
detail: In selectOutreach's call() (app.js ~364-377), a successful action does toast('done'); loadOutreach(); -- the list reloads but #outreachDetail is neither cleared nor re-rendered, and oState.selected keeps pointing at the row. Concrete scenario: operator opens Drafts, selects draft X, clicks 'Approve for sending' (row becomes 'approved' and leaves the drafts folder), then notices a typo in the still-open editor, fixes it, and clicks 'Approve for sending' again. The PATCH /api/outreach/{id} hits the status='drafted' guard in outreach_edit (main.py 315-329) and returns 409 'only drafts can be edited'; call() throws before the decision POST. The fix is never persisted anywhere, yet the editor keeps displaying the corrected text and the status pill still says 'drafted', so the operator reasonably believes the on-screen text is what was approved. The next 'python tools/outreach.py send' mails the earlier, typo'd version -- and Invariant 5 means that company can never be emailed again. Same stale-panel mechanism produces spurious 409 toasts after Cancel draft / Withdraw approval (buttons remain live on a row whose state changed), and the identical lost-edit scenario occurs with two browser tabs: tab B edits a draft that tab A already approved, clicks approve, gets 409, edits discarded. Fix: after a successful action, re-fetch the row (or clear the panel / re-render from the reloaded folder) instead of leaving the old DOM with live buttons.
why_real: Verified against source. (1) app.js:364-377 call() success path is toast("done"); loadOutreach(); and loadOutreach() (293-322) only rewrites #folderBar/#outreachBody — #outreachDetail is cleared solely in the folder-switch handler (303-305), so the panel keeps stale DOM with live buttons and oState.selected keeps the id. (2) outreach_folders view (sql/20_outreach.sql:93-94) maps drafted→drafts, approved→outbox, so the approved row vanishes from the reloaded Drafts list while the panel still shows the draft editor and 'drafted' pill. (3) Second Approve after a client-side edit PATCHes /api/outreach/{id}; outreach_edit (main.py:315-329) updates only where status='drafted', fetchone() is None, raises 409 'only drafts can be edited'; api() throws (app.js:27-35), the catch toasts, the decision POST never runs, nothing re-renders — the fix is persisted nowhere while looking saved. (4) tools/outreach.py:242 sends where status='approved', i.e. the earlier typo'd text saved by the first approve. (5) Invariant 5 is real: uq_outreach_one_touch partial unique index (sql/20_outreach.sql:59-62) on outreach(entity_id) where direction='outbound' and status not in ('cancelled','failed') — a 'sent' row stays covered, so a corrective second email is schema-impossible. (6) Repeat Cancel/Withdraw on the stale panel hits main.py:344-346 (status in ('drafted','approved')), returns no row, raises 409 'row is not in a state that allows cancel' (362-363) — the spurious-toast claim holds. (7) Two-tab lost-edit variant follows from the same status='drafted' guard. No compensating mechanism (polling, panel refresh) exists. Cited line numbers are accurate.

title: Out-of-order loadOutreach responses render one folder's rows under another folder's active pill
detail: loadOutreach (app.js 293-322) has no request-sequencing token and never aborts an in-flight fetch. The URL captures oState.folder at invocation, but the render reads oState.folder at completion. Concrete scenario: operator clicks the 'Drafts' pill then quickly the 'Sent' pill (or clicks 'Mark positive' in Replies -- whose call() fires loadOutreach for 'inbox' -- then immediately clicks the 'Positive' pill). Two fetches are in flight; if the older one (drafts/inbox) resolves last, it overwrites oState.rows and #outreachBody with the OLD folder's rows while the folder bar re-renders with the NEW folder highlighted (key === oState.folder uses the current value). Result: 'Sent' pill shown active over the Drafts listing; clicking a row opens a draft editor with an 'Approve for sending' button while the operator believes they are browsing sent mail. Self-heals only on the next pill click. Fix: a monotonically increasing request id checked before rendering, or AbortController on folder change.
why_real: Confirmed by re-derivation from app/static/app.js. loadOutreach (lines 293-322) bakes oState.folder into the fetch URL at invocation (line 295) but renders at completion using the then-current oState.folder for the pill highlight (lines 299-301) while filling #outreachBody and oState.rows from the fetched response d.rows (lines 297, 307). The api() helper (lines 27-35) is a bare fetch wrapper with no AbortController, and grep confirms no sequencing token or abort anywhere in the file. The pill handler (lines 303-305) mutates oState.folder and fires a new loadOutreach without cancelling the in-flight one, so two concurrent fetches exist and the later-resolving one wins the DOM. If the older folder's response resolves last, the new folder's pill shows active over the old folder's rows, and a row click (selectOutreach, lines 324+) reads the stale oState.rows — for a drafts row this renders the draft editor with the 'Approve for sending' button (lines 343-351) under e.g. an active 'Sent' pill. The 'Mark positive' variant also checks out: call() (line 376) fires loadOutreach for the current inbox folder, and an immediate 'Positive' pill click creates the same race. Only nit: it self-heals on any subsequent loadOutreach trigger (tab re-entry, decision), not only a pill click — immaterial to the finding.

title: Correcting a mis-triaged reply (positive -> negative) leaves the company stuck in in_conversation with no undo path
detail: The UI keeps 'Mark positive' and 'Mark negative' buttons live on already-triaged replies (app.js 354-357 shows them for any inbound row not cancelled), and outreach_decide (main.py 347-359) allows re-triage: mark_positive promotes the entity from 'contacted' to 'in_conversation', but mark_negative performs no entity update at all. Concrete scenario: operator fat-fingers 'Mark positive' on a decline reply -- the entity is immediately moved to in_conversation -- then clicks 'Mark negative' to correct it. The outreach row flips to triage='negative', but the entity stays 'in_conversation' forever: no endpoint, button, or CLI command reverts it, and 'in_conversation' is outside OPEN_STATUSES so the company also vanishes from the review queue. The state the whole engine exists to produce is now recorded for a company that said no, and fixing it requires hand-written SQL. Fix: mark_negative should demote the entity back to 'contacted' when its status is 'in_conversation' (mirroring the guarded promotion), or the promotion should be deferred/confirmed.
why_real: Verified against the source. app.js:354-357 renders 'Mark positive'/'Mark negative' for any inbound row not cancelled, so triaged replies keep live buttons. main.py:349-351 updates the outreach row with only `direction='inbound'` as a filter (no status guard), so re-triage succeeds. Lines 353-356 promote the entity contacted->in_conversation only on the positive label; mark_negative performs no entity write. The scenario re-derives exactly: mis-click positive on a decline promotes the entity; the corrective mark_negative flips outreach.triage but leaves the entity in_conversation permanently. No revert path exists: tools/outreach.py:273 only sets contacted where status='shortlisted'; tools/apply_verification.py:93-96 explicitly leaves in_conversation rows alone; sql/13_apply_gates.sql only archives open-status rows (its in_conversation mention is a report-only SELECT); and the entity is invisible in the review UI since in_conversation is outside OPEN_STATUSES (main.py:41). Two minor caveats that do not defeat the finding: (1) /api/leads/{id}/decision (main.py:242-266) has no status guard, so a hand-crafted curl with the entity UUID could move the entity to shortlisted/rejected/ready_for_review — but never back to 'contacted', so no true revert exists and a correct fix does require hand SQL; (2) 'vanishes from the review queue' is slightly overstated since a contacted entity was already outside OPEN_STATUSES before the mis-click.

title: Action buttons never disabled during in-flight requests; double-clicking Approve shows a success toast followed by an error toast
detail: call() in selectOutreach (app.js 364-378) does not disable #oApprove/#oCancel/#oPos/#oNeg while its two sequential requests run. Concrete scenario: operator double-clicks 'Approve for sending'. Click 1 runs PATCH (saves edits) then POST approve (status -> approved). Click 2's PATCH or POST then hits a state guard -- either 409 'only drafts can be edited' or 409 'row is not in a state that allows approve' -- so the operator sees toast 'done' immediately replaced by a red error toast for the very row they just approved. The approval actually succeeded (server guards hold, no duplicate send is possible thanks to the status machine and Invariant 5), but the operator cannot tell whether it worked and may go hunting for a phantom failure. Both interleavings (PATCH1/POST1/PATCH2 and PATCH1/PATCH2/POST1/POST2) end in the spurious error. Fix: disable the buttons on first click until call() settles.
why_real: Verified against source. app.js:364-378 defines call() with no disabling, no in-flight guard, no debounce; listeners at 379-382 are bare click handlers, and a repo-wide grep shows the only disabled usage is pagination (app.js:151-152) — nothing ever disables #oApprove/#oCancel/#oPos/#oNeg. A double-click fires two click events milliseconds apart, before any fetch settles, so a second concurrent call("approve","approve") launches. Server guards match the claim exactly: PATCH outreach_edit (main.py:325-328) 409s "only drafts can be edited" when status != drafted, and the approve decision (main.py:341-342, 362-363) 409s "row is not in a state that allows approve" once status is approved. cursor() (main.py:59-72) commits per request on an 8-connection pool; under READ COMMITTED the second concurrent conditional UPDATE re-evaluates after the first commits and matches 0 rows, so exactly one approve succeeds and the other request 409s in both interleavings (PATCH1/POST1/PATCH2 -> edit 409; PATCH1/PATCH2/POST1/POST2 -> approve 409). Client UX matches: api() surfaces the JSON detail as the error message, click 1 shows toast("done"), click 2's catch overwrites the same #toast element with the 409 text styled red via .toast.err (style.css:224). The approval genuinely succeeds server-side (no duplicate transition), but the operator sees a spurious error for the row they just approved. Only trivial imprecision: call() makes two requests only on the approve path, which is the path the scenario uses.
